hero.heading: I study what happens where two materials meet.
hero.definition: Ice on road surfaces, bitumen on stone, salt in freezing water. I model these interfaces molecule by molecule and test the models against experiments.

how_i_work.heading: I solve problems.
how_i_work.text: I connect molecular behaviour to mechanisms and measurable material response through simulation, theory and experimental validation. I also scoped and led a modelling subtask in a national highway-safety R&D programme, setting its computing needs, budget and schedule.
how_i_work.question: Does shaking help water freeze?
how_i_work.answer: It depends on how you shake it.

how_i_work.heading: I make work easier.
how_i_work.text: I build reusable simulation workflows and analysis tools, and automate large simulation campaigns on national computing systems, which cut submission time by about 80%. I also designed a shared research database used by about 15 researchers and managed its external developer.
how_i_work.question: How do scattered tasks become a repeatable workflow?
how_i_work.answer: A clear sequence makes repeated work easier.

how_i_work.heading: I help others understand.
how_i_work.text: I explain complex results through scientific visualisation, presentations and mentoring. I have mentored MEng and BEng thesis students and tutored four undergraduate engineering courses.
how_i_work.question: How can a complex idea become easy to understand?
how_i_work.answer: Residence time is the average time something stays in a place before leaving.

about.text: My research connects surface design, adhesion and ice nucleation. I combine molecular simulation, laboratory experiments and scientific computing to understand interfaces and address practical environmental questions. So far: 8 peer-reviewed papers (4 first-author), 400 citations and about 800,000 compute units on UK national supercomputers.
